pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants? (1 mark)
   A. They give plastic
   B. They cause floods
   C. They give food, shade and wood
   D. They make noise

2. Why should you not pull leaves off a young plant for fun? (1 mark)
   A. The plant needs its leaves to make food
   B. The plant has too many leaves
   C. The leaves make the roots sweet
   D. Leaves are heavy

3. Which of these do plants need to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Only sand
   B. Stones and plastic
   C. Only darkness
   D. Water, air and light

4. Which part of the plant holds it firmly in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Roots
   B. Flowers
   C. Fruit
   D. Leaves

5. Which of these gives the young plant its first food before its leaves open? (1 mark)
   A. The seed
   B. The flower
   C. The wind
   D. The bark

6. What does the stem do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes food using sunlight
   B. Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   C. Only takes in water
   D. Makes seeds

7. Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school? (1 mark)
   A. Water them when the soil is dry
   B. Trample on flower beds
   C. Pick all the flowers
   D. Throw litter on them

8. Maize lives for one season and then dies. A baobab lives for many years. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Maize never grows
   B. Only maize is alive
   C. Baobab does not die
   D. Plants live for different lengths of time

9. Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Roots
   B. Stem
   C. Seed coat
   D. Flower

10. Which animal group breathes using gills? (1 mark)
   A. Mammals
   B. Reptiles
   C. Fish
   D. Birds

11. Which of these do animals breathe in from the air? (1 mark)
   A. Oxygen
   B. Dust
   C. Smoke
   D. Water

12. Which of these is a sign of life in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding
   B. Staying in one place forever
   C. Being painted
   D. Being made of metal

13. What is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal without bones
   B. An animal with a backbone
   C. An animal with six legs
   D. An animal that lives in water only

14. How do young mammals get their first food? (1 mark)
   A. By drinking their mother's milk
   B. By eating stones
   C. By hunting
   D. By eating grass

15. Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach ache
   B. Sunburn
   C. Sneezing
   D. A headache only

16. What should you do when you have a persistent stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Eat more sweets
   B. Tell an adult and see a health worker
   C. Hide it
   D. Drink dirty water

17. Why should fruits and vegetables be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To remove dirt and germs
   B. To make them sweeter
   C. To make them heavier
   D. To make them hot

18. Why should you wear shoes and wash hands to prevent worms? (1 mark)
   A. Worms live in shoes
   B. Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   C. Water makes worms grow
   D. Shoes make food digest

19. Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Anus
   C. Gullet
   D. Large intestine

20. Why should you chew your food well? (1 mark)
   A. It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   B. It stops you drinking water
   C. It makes food colder
   D. It makes food heavier

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples. (4 marks)

22. Name two invertebrates that are found near your school. (2 marks)

23. Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week. (5 marks)

24. Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it. (5 marks)

25. Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways. (5 marks)

26. Describe what happens to food in the stomach. (3 marks)

27. Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light. (4 marks)

28. State any four signs of life in animals. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — They give food, shade and wood
   Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

2. A — The plant needs its leaves to make food
   Leaves are the food factories of the plant.

3. D — Water, air and light
   Plants need water, air, light and nutrients from the soil.

4. A — Roots
   Roots anchor the plant in the ground.

5. A — The seed
   The seed contains stored food that feeds the young plant at first.

6. B — Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   The stem supports the plant and carries water and food.

7. A — Water them when the soil is dry
   Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

8. D — Plants live for different lengths of time
   All plants die, but some live for one season and others for many years.

9. A — Roots
   Roots take in water and mineral salts.

10. C — Fish
   Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

11. A — Oxygen
   Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

12. A — Feeding
   Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

13. B — An animal with a backbone
   Vertebrates have a backbone.

14. A — By drinking their mother's milk
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

15. A — Stomach ache
   Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

16. B — Tell an adult and see a health worker
   Adults and health workers can help find the cause.

17. A — To remove dirt and germs
   Washing removes dirt, germs and worm eggs.

18. B — Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   Worm eggs can enter the body through dirt.

19. D — Large intestine
   The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

20. A — It makes food smaller for easier digestion
   Chewing breaks food into small pieces.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two correct examples such as ant, earthworm, snail, butterfly, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct invertebrate.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.
